newsitem.title: CANADA: NOVA sees no major costs from GasAndes dispute.
newsitem.headline: NOVA sees no major costs from GasAndes dispute.

text.p: NOVA Corp President Jeff Lipton said on Tuesday he expected no major costs from a legal dispute that has delayed testing of the Argentina-Chile GasAndes pipeline, slated for an August 7 opening.
"We are working hard, both physically and legally, to overcome some legal hurdles which may cause a minor delay in our planned opening," Lipton said in a conference call.
"We do not anticipate any significant costs associated with this possible delay and may be able to complete the construction work necessary to remove the injunction by the end of July," he said.
The US$325 million pipeline project is co-led by NOVA and Chilgener SA. It would initially ship 120 million cubic feet a day of gas to Santiago from Menoza in central Argentina.
Shipments were expected to reach 700 million cubic feet a day by 2001.

But work on the project was delayed last week after a Chilean court ordered an injunction pending new studies on mud and rockslide prevention at San Alfonso, Chile. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
